question.problem: A fair die has $9$ sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $9.$ What is the probability of getting a number greater than or equal to $6$ on the next throw of the die?
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number the die lands on. From the problem statement, we know that $X \sim U \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\},$ and we wish to compute $P(X \geq 6).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129053/assets/04a4d9a4cad75503f6dead488d088b95d9e44cde6ca44e73a33cb4e5a242111d.svg)

Here, we have $X \sim U \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\},$ and the set $S = \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}$ has $|S| = 9-1 + 1 = 9$ items. So, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129053/assets/c34845ee8e867275c17efed55359d7fea4414e2688c25356b28df73c48c974f9.svg)

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $X \geq 6$ are $6, 7, 8, 9.$ Since there are $4$ elements in total, we have

$$
P(X \geq 6) = 4 \cdot \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{4}{9}.
$$
